newsitem.title: USA: FCOJ futures end higher, Sept under resistance.
newsitem.headline: FCOJ futures end higher, Sept under resistance.

text.p: FCOJ futures ended the day higher amid light speculative buying, but trade selling kept the benchmark September contract below its upside target of 76.00 cents, market sources said.
The overall trend remains to the downside as supplies in both the U.S. and in Brazil swell and demand for juice remains flat, they said.
The benchmark September contract closed 0.90 cent higher at 75.35 cents a lb, having ranged from 76.00 to 74.30 cents. The rest of the board settled 0.75 lower to to 1.10 higher.
An estimated 2,000 lots changed hands on the day, compared with Friday's official 916 lots.
Near-term support remains at 74.00 cents followed by 73.50 cents in September. Longer term, the spot month could ease to 70.00-65.00 cents, analysts said.

PaineWebber analyst Bernard Savaiko said the market may have put in an intermediate-term bottom but added that the September contract will need to close above 76.00 cents, the high made July 10 and July 15, to climb higher.
"The chart looks lower but for the past couple of days we've closed over a downtrend line dating back to mid-May," Savaiko said. "A close over 76.00 cents could signal near-term gains."
Resistance over 76.00 cents was pegged at 78.25 cents, followed by 82.45 cents.
